vendors.name: Dremio
vendors.tagline: Iceberg lakehouse and query engine; semantic layer is views, wikis, and labels.
vendors.verdictNote: Views, wikis, labels, and semantic search give an AI agent business context, but Dremio has no metric, dimension, or relationship objects.

metrics.n: No metric object found in docs. Metric logic lives as SQL expressions inside views.

dimensions.n: No declared dimensions or hierarchies found in docs. Views expose plain columns.

relationships.n: No declared join paths found in docs. Joins are written inside view SQL.

synonyms.n: Markdown wikis and labels on datasets and folders. The AI Agent reads them as context.

verifiedQueries.n: No verified-query or example-SQL store found in the docs.

nl2sql.n: Built-in AI Agent writes SQL, charts, and explanations. Needs the CALL MODEL privilege; built-in or external LLM.

ontology.n: No ontology layer. Spaces, folders, views, wikis, and labels are the modeling objects.

graph.n: No graph query language found. A lineage graph exists for datasets only.

vector.n: AI semantic search over names, wikis, labels, and metadata. English-optimized; index can lag a few hours.

mcp.n: Hosted MCP server with OAuth, plus self-hosted open-source server. Tools include RunSqlQuery and GetSchemaOfTable.

governance.n: Agent acts with the user's privileges. Row-access and column-masking policies apply to views. Dataset-level lineage is available.

openStandard.n: Listed in Apache Ossie ecosystem, but no Dremio converter or export found. Catalog follows Iceberg REST on Apache Polaris.

offers: Views in spaces and folders, layered as preparation, business, and application, give agents curated tables to query.
Markdown wikis and labels on datasets add descriptions that the AI Agent reads for discovery and SQL generation.
Hosted MCP server with OAuth lets Claude or ChatGPT query governed data under the user's own privileges.
Built-in AI Agent turns questions into SQL and charts, and explains SQL or past jobs inside the console.
Row-access and column-masking policies on tables and views are applied by the query planner at run time.
Semantic search finds tables, views, and folders from natural-language terms using names, wikis, and labels.
gaps: No metric, dimension, or join-path objects. Business logic stays inside view SQL, so agents must infer joins and metric rules.
AI generation of wikis and labels is Preview. Docs warn that table names, tags, and wikis may reach the model.
No verified question-to-SQL store, no ontology layer, and no graph query language found.
No Dremio converter for Apache Ossie found, so semantic definitions are not portable.
The self-hosted MCP server is open source and outside Dremio support policies.
fillWith: Apache Ossie YAML (spec only, no Dremio converter found)
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model business logic as business-layer views, then write a wiki and labels for each view and column. Point the AI Agent or the hosted MCP server at that space. Put metric formulas and join rules in the wikis, because Dremio has no object for them.

snippet.title: A view in a space, from the CREATE VIEW reference (wikis and labels are edited in the console, REST API, or CLI)
snippet.code:
-- Dremio docs example: a view stored in a space or folder
CREATE VIEW demo.jobs_view AS SELECT * FROM "oracle_e2e".DREMIO.JOBS

vendors.name: Denodo Platform
vendors.tagline: Logical data management platform with a semantic layer of views, associations, and metric views.
vendors.verdictNote: Since 9.5 (July 2026), metric views plus associations and view metadata form a semantic layer, and the Data Marketplace assistant queries metric views.

artifacts.name: View and column descriptions, tags, and associations
Denodo Assistant (VQL Shell and Data Marketplace)
Denodo AI SDK (text-to-VQL, metadata search, open source)
Vector data type and metadata embeddings

metrics.n: Metric views (9.5, July 2026) declare metrics over fact and dimension views, reusable across BI and AI.

dimensions.n: Metric views declare dimensions and dimension groups. No hierarchy or time-grain clause found in the syntax.

relationships.n: Associations declare joins between views. Metric views list them in an ASSOCIATIONS clause with a join type.

synonyms.n: View and column descriptions, tags, logical names, and Assistant custom instructions. No dedicated synonym field found.

verifiedQueries.n: No verified question-to-SQL store found in the AI SDK manual or the 9.4 and 9.5 release notes.

nl2sql.n: Denodo Assistant and metric view assisted query write VQL; open-source AI SDK adds text-to-VQL. You supply the LLM.

ontology.n: No ontology layer. Views, associations, and metric views are the modeling objects. 360 Graph maps assets and lineage.

graph.n: No graph query language found. 360 Graph (renamed from Reference Lineage) is a lineage and asset map.

vector.n: Vector data type with distance functions (9.4). Metadata search needs a configured external vector database such as PGVector.

mcp.n: Standalone read-only MCP server and AI SDK MCP endpoint. Tools include run_vql_query, metadata_search, generate_vql.

governance.n: Denodo privileges are the final filter for MCP. AI SDK retrieves only views the user may access. Tags set visibility.

openStandard.n: Listed in the Apache Ossie ecosystem and working group, but no converter or Ossie export found.

offers: Metric views define KPIs once over joined views; the Data Marketplace assistant turns plain-language requests into VQL against them.
Open-source AI SDK provides text-to-VQL, vector metadata search, and a DeepQuery agent for multi-step questions.
Standalone read-only MCP server exposes view metadata, semantic metadata search, and tools to validate and run VQL.
Views carry descriptions, tags, and associations. The AI SDK passes this schema to the LLM and filters by user permission.
One virtual layer reaches many sources, so agents query live data without copying it.
gaps: Metric views are new (9.5, July 2026). The AI SDK and MCP docs do not mention them.
No ontology, verified-query store, or graph query language found.
Metadata search and the AI SDK need an external vector database and an LLM that you configure and run.
9.5 docs list AI and Semantics feature packs under Enterprise Plus. Licensing scope was not checked.
The manual says the sample chatbot is not for production, and Chroma is for demos only.
fillWith: PGVector or OpenSearch as the metadata vector store
Apache Ossie (Denodo is a listed participant, no converter found)
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Model facts and dimensions as metric views, fill in view and column descriptions, and tag the views. Then run the Denodo AI SDK or MCP server with a vector store you host, so the LLM sees view schemas and descriptions. Use DeepQuery only for multi-step questions, because it needs a thinking model with at least 128k context.

snippet.title: Metric view in VQL (shortened from the 9.5 VQL Guide example)
snippet.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE METRIC VIEW sales_view
  DESCRIPTION = 'Example of metric view'
  SOURCES (
    orders AS vdb_tpch.psql_tpch_orders,
    customer AS vdb_tpch.psql_tpch_customer )
  ASSOCIATIONS (
    orders customer vdb_tpch.psql_tpch_customer_psql_tpch_orders INNER )
  DIMENSIONS (
    customer_dim( customer_name AS customer.c_name ),
    order_date AS orders.o_orderdate )
  METRICS (
    count_order_keys AS count(orders.o_orderkey),
    order_average_value AS avg(orders.o_totalprice) );

vendors.name: Starburst / Trino
vendors.tagline: Trino-based federated query engine with data products, an AI agent, and an MCP server.
vendors.verdictNote: Data products (views plus descriptions, tags, sample queries, and business rules) feed the AI agent, but there are no metric, dimension, or relationship objects, and open-source Trino has none of it.

artifacts.name: Data product (views and materialized views in a schema)
Data product business rules (businessContext)
artifacts.format: Free text in GUI or YAML

artifacts.name: AI Data Assistant (AIDA), powered by the Starburst AI agent
AIDA skills and external MCP servers

metrics.n: No metric object. Metric rules go in view SQL or in free-text business rules that AIDA reads.

dimensions.n: No dimension or hierarchy objects. Columns and column descriptions are the only structure.

relationships.n: No declared join paths. Dataset descriptions can explain relations in free text.

synonyms.n: Data product and column descriptions, tags, and business rules (up to 60,000 characters) give AIDA context.

verifiedQueries.n: Data products store sample queries. AIDA uses only their descriptions as suggested prompts, not the SQL as few-shot context.

nl2sql.n: AIDA turns questions into SQL over a chosen data product. GA since 477-e; needs AI workflows and agentic-layer licenses.

ontology.n: No ontology. Data products group into domains, but no entity or class model was found.

graph.n: No graph query language found in the Starburst or Trino docs.

vector.n: AI functions include starburst.ai.generate_embedding(). No native vector index found; data product search is keyword.

mcp.n: Integrated MCP server, GA since 477-e: read-only query tool plus data product search and retrieval. Needs an MCP license.

governance.n: AIDA runs under the user's role and logs agent interactions. Data product privileges grant no table access.

openStandard.n: Data Products as Code is Starburst-specific YAML (sep/v1). Starburst Data is listed in the Ossie ecosystem; no converter found.

offers: Data products bundle views with descriptions, tags, owners, sample queries, and business rules. AIDA reads them as context.
AIDA generates and runs SQL over a chosen data product, with personas and an audit log of agent interactions.
Integrated MCP server (GA since 477-e) offers read-only query plus data product search and retrieval tools.
Agent-based enrichment drafts descriptions for data products, datasets, and columns from schema, SQL, and optional data samples.
Data Products as Code exports and imports data products as YAML, which supports versioning and auditing.
gaps: No metric, dimension, or join-path objects. Metric logic lives in view SQL or free-text business rules.
Open-source Trino has no semantic layer; views accept only a COMMENT. Data products, AIDA, and MCP are Starburst products.
Data products need a Hive or Iceberg catalog. AIDA and MCP need separate licenses.
AIDA skills, external MCP servers, and data sampling in enrichment are public preview (August 2026).
No documented use of sample queries as AI context, and no native vector search.
fillWith: Apache Ossie (Starburst Data is listed, no converter found)
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Build data products on Hive or Iceberg catalogs, write column descriptions and business rules, then use AIDA or the Starburst MCP server against those products. Put metric formulas in business rules or view SQL, because no metric object exists. On open-source Trino, you must build the semantic context yourself, for example with dbt or Cube.

snippet.title: Data Products as Code excerpt (shortened; publishing also needs summary and owners)
snippet.code:
apiVersion: sep/v1
kind: DataProduct
metadata:
  name: Comprehensive Data Product
  catalogName: analytics_catalog
  dataDomainName: Enterprise Analytics Domain
  businessContext: Revenue is gross_sales - returns - discounts in USD.
datasets:
  views:
    - name: sales_summary
      definitionQuery: SELECT product_id, SUM(amount) AS total_revenue FROM raw.transactions.sales GROUP BY 1
      columns:
        - name: total_revenue
          type: decimal(18,2)
          description: Total revenue in USD

vendors.name: Timbr.ai
vendors.tagline: SQL-native ontology and virtual knowledge graph over existing SQL sources, with data agents and MCP.
vendors.verdictNote: Concepts, relationships, measures, cubes, and a Knowledge Base of approved examples are first-party objects that Timbr's own agents and MCP server read.

artifacts.name: Mapping (CREATE MAPPING) from source tables to concepts
Virtual knowledge graph and graph algorithms (gtimbr)

metrics.n: CREATE MEASURE defines aggregations with filters and temporal variants. Measures feed cubes.

dimensions.n: Cubes expose properties of a concept and related concepts as dimensions; grouping is chosen at query time.

relationships.n: Relationships are foreign-key constraints with inverse names. One-to-many, many-to-many, and transitive forms exist.

synonyms.n: Concept descriptions, tags, and Knowledge Base instructions that define business terms. No dedicated synonym field found.

verifiedQueries.n: Knowledge Base holds approved question-SQL examples. Agents reuse or follow them before generating SQL.

nl2sql.n: Data agents, Ask Timbr, and the LangChain SDK generate Timbr SQL over the ontology with your LLM.

ontology.n: SQL-native ontology: concepts with inheritance, relationships, and inference, exposed as a virtual schema over JDBC, ODBC, REST.

graph.n: Graph traversal in SQL and graph algorithms in the gtimbr schema. No SPARQL or Cypher found in the docs.

vector.n: No vector index or embedding search found in the docs. GraphRAG Extract maps entities from unstructured data.

mcp.n: First-party MCP server with API key or OAuth. Tools include query_data, generate_sql, describe_knowledge_graph, execute_sql.

governance.n: RBAC on ontologies, agents, and Knowledge Bases, plus row-level security policies that also cover views.

openStandard.n: No Ossie listing found. Intro says ERD and OWL import exists; ontology Git export arrived in 2.69.0 (Oct 2026).

offers: Ontology of concepts, relationships, and measures over many SQL sources, so agents write short semantic SQL instead of joins.
Knowledge Base stores approved question-SQL examples and rules that agents look up before they generate SQL.
MCP server exposes natural-language tools (query_data, generate_sql) and metadata tools (describe_knowledge_graph, list_ontologies).
Cubes and measures define aggregations once and serve SQL and BI tools over JDBC, ODBC, and REST.
Row-level security policies and RBAC apply to ontologies, agents, and Knowledge Bases.
gaps: Ontology DDL is Timbr-specific SQL. No Ossie or OSI support found, so models are not portable.
AI features need a customer-provided LLM. MCP docs say outputs are probabilistic and need review.
No vector or embedding search found in the docs.
Docs give no GA or beta label for MCP or Knowledge Base. Solomon is in private preview.
Graph support is SQL traversal and algorithms; no SPARQL or Cypher found.
vendors.nl2sqlPath: Map your sources to concepts, add relationships and measures, and describe each concept. Create a Knowledge Base of approved examples and bind it to the ontology or to a data agent. Then connect an LLM through a data agent, the LangChain SDK, or the MCP server.

snippet.title: Concept with a relationship (placeholders as written in the Timbr docs)
snippet.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE CONCEPT `{concept_name}` (
  `{property_name}` {property_type},
  `{property_name2}` {property_type2},
  PRIMARY KEY(`{property_name}`),
  LABEL(`{property_name2}`),
  CONSTRAINT `{relationship_name}`
    FOREIGN KEY (`{property_name2}`)
    REFERENCES `{target_concept}` (`{target_concept_property}`)
    INVERSEOF `{inverse_relationship_name}`
) INHERITS (`{inherits_from_concept}`)
DESCRIPTION '{concept_description}';

notes.topic: Open Semantic Interchange is now Apache Ossie (incubating)
notes.text: The OSI project is renamed Apache Ossie and is in the Apache Incubator. The Ossie ecosystem page lists Denodo, Dremio, and Starburst Data. It does not list Timbr, and it shows no converter for any of the four.

sources.t: Dremio: Apache Ossie, the new name for Open Semantic Interchange (13 Jul 2026)

notes.topic: Dremio is now part of SAP
notes.text: SAP announced completion of the Dremio acquisition on 6 July 2026. Dremio docs and press pages still use the Dremio name, and a site banner reads 'Dremio is now part of SAP'. No rename was announced in the docs.

notes.topic: Dremio docs split and agentic lakehouse timeline
notes.text: Dremio Cloud (launched 13 Nov 2025 as the agentic lakehouse) and self-managed Dremio have separate doc trees. The current/ tree is the self-managed 26.x docs. The Nov 2025 launch named the AI Semantic Layer, AI Agent, and MCP support but gave no per-feature GA label.

sources.t: Dremio unveils the agentic lakehouse (13 Nov 2025)

notes.text: Data Catalog became Data Marketplace in 9.3. Embedded MPP became Lakehouse Accelerator and Cache Engine became Materialization Engine by 9.4. Reference Lineage became 360 Graph in 9.5.
9.3 shipped 16 Sep 2025 with DeepQuery. 9.4 (March 2026, vector data type) and 9.5 (July 2026, metric views, LLM-agent Denodo Assistant) dates come from press coverage, not Denodo docs.

notes.topic: Status labels used in this file
notes.text: Vendors in this set label Preview features in their docs (Dremio wiki generation, Starburst skills, Timbr Solomon). Features with no label in their own doc page are marked GA here. Where a release note or press release states GA, the artifact says so; otherwise treat GA as inferred from the missing Preview label.

sources.t: Dremio wikis and labels (Preview label on AI generation)

notes.text: The docs cover mostly Starburst Enterprise 483-e. Starburst Galaxy also documents AIDA, AI data product enrichment, and an MCP server, but its release status is unverified. Open-source Trino views accept a COMMENT clause and nothing else for semantic context.

notes.topic: Timbr MCP and Knowledge Base timing
notes.text: The Timbr changelog shows MCP OAuth and Dynamic Client Registration in release 2.55.1 (23 Mar 2026). It shows a new Knowledge Base management page in the 14 Jul 2026 release. The first MCP release date was not found.

The Dremio docs say the open-source MCP server is not covered by Dremio Support Policies. The hosted server needs a Dremio Cloud project and, for clients other than Claude.ai and ChatGPT, a Native OAuth application.
